common_date.description: A calendar date in ISO 8601 form, YYYY-MM-DD.

decisionId.description: A decision's four-digit number, the prefix of its name, quoted so leading zeros survive ("0009", not 0009).

decision_schema.description: The YAML frontmatter of a decision record, NNNN-slug.md in the repository's decisions directory (EC-0021). The record's name carries its number, so the frontmatter does not repeat it. DEC-02 checks a record's frontmatter against this schema.

amended_by.description: Decisions that change this one in part. The status is unchanged: an amended decision is still in force.

amends.description: Decisions this one changes in part, leaving the rest in force. Each lists this one in amended_by (DEC-04).

consulted.description: Whose opinion was sought before deciding.

date.description: When the decision reached its current status.

deciders.description: Who made the decision. MADR 4 calls this field decision-makers; the name here is kept (EC-0021).

informed.description: Who is kept up to date on the decision.

status.description: proposed: open for comment; accepted: in force; rejected: considered and declined; deprecated: no longer applies; superseded: replaced by the decisions in superseded_by.

superseded_by.description: Decisions that replace this one. Required once the status is superseded, and set only then (DEC-04).

supersedes.description: Decisions this one replaces. Each lists this one in superseded_by (DEC-04).

decision_schema.title: Decision record frontmatter

common_date.description: A calendar date in ISO 8601 form, YYYY-MM-DD.

common_displayForms.description: Display forms keyed by lower-case identifier token: how the token is written in a Title-Cased name, e.g. api: API.

common_pathGlob.description: A repository-relative glob with forward slashes: * matches within one path segment, ** matches across segments.

common_requirementId.description: A requirement identifier: a registered family prefix, a hyphen and a two- or three-digit number, e.g. GHA-07. Append-only and never reused.

common_slug.description: A lower-case kebab-case identifier, e.g. github-actions.

common_version.description: A release version in MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH form, without a leading v, e.g. 0.1.0.

expires.description: The last day the waiver applies, as a quoted "YYYY-MM-DD" string (an unquoted TOML date is rejected), at most 180 days ahead.

paths.description: Limit the waiver to findings on these paths (repository-relative globs). Omit to waive the requirement everywhere.

reason.description: Why the deviation is needed, in at least 20 characters.

requirement.description: The requirement waived. ADOPT requirements cannot be waived.

tracking.description: The issue that tracks removing the waiver.

declaration_schema.description: A consuming repository's optional .repo/conventions.toml: the convention profile that applies to it and every waiver it holds, and, for a repository that does not pin the release in mise, the release it is checked against. ADOPT-02 checks a declaration against this schema.

adoption.description: A staged adoption: while it is in force, only findings in the listed families (and always ADOPT) count toward --fail-on; the rest are reported as not enforced. Once it expires, every family is enforced (ADOPT-10, ADOPT-11).

enforce.description: The requirement families enforced, by ID prefix, e.g. ["ADOPT", "REPO", "OUT", "GHA"].

expires.description: The last day the staged adoption applies, as a quoted "YYYY-MM-DD" string, at most 180 days ahead. After it, every family is enforced.

tracking.description: The issue that tracks enforcing the remaining families.

conventions.description: Which release of musher-dev/engineering-conventions this repository is checked against. Optional when mise pins the release (github:musher-dev/engineering-conventions).

version.description: The pinned release, without a leading v, e.g. 0.1.0.

decisions.description: Where the repository keeps its decision records, when not in docs/decisions/ as one NNNN-slug.md file each (EC-0021).

form.description: file: each record is <path>/NNNN-slug.md and the index is <path>/README.md. directory: each record is <path>/NNNN-slug/<page> and the index is <path>/<page>. Defaults to file.

page.description: In the directory form, the name of the Markdown file each record's directory holds, which is also the index's name, e.g. +page.md. Defaults to README.md. The file form ignores it.

path.description: The directory that holds the records, relative to the repository root, e.g. docs/adrs. Its last segment is decisions or adrs, the names the runner reads records from. Defaults to docs/decisions.

paths.description: How the checks treat parts of the repository.

fixtures.description: Directories of test fixtures: sample repositories and deliberately invalid files that a test reads. The checks do not read them as part of this repository. Declare only fixtures here; a finding in real code needs a waiver, which expires.

profile.description: The convention profile that applies, e.g. base-repo. Defaults to base-repo.

schema_version.description: Version of this file's shape. Always 1.

vocabulary.description: Repository-specific vocabulary on top of the release's.

display_forms.description: Extra display forms, keyed by lower-case token, e.g. grpc = "gRPC". They add to the release's display forms.

waivers.description: Time-boxed, tracked deviations from a requirement. Requirements in the ADOPT family cannot be waived.

declaration_schema.title: Conventions declaration

common_slug.description: A lower-case kebab-case identifier, e.g. github-actions.

description.description: One line on what this repository uses it for.

fetched.description: True when the repository fetches the release's assets at test or build time and verifies them against the release's SHA256SUMS, instead of vendoring them. A fetched dependency has no vendored copy, so DEPS-05 and DEPS-06 skip it.

interfaces.description: The ids of the producer's interfaces this repository vendors; all of the output's interfaces when omitted.

output.description: The id of the producer's output that delivers the interfaces, e.g. contracts.

repository.description: The producing repository's name on GitHub, without the organization, e.g. platform-api.

version.description: The exact release version pinned, without a leading v, e.g. 0.36.1. The only copy of the pin (DEPS-04).

dependencies_schema.description: A repository's .repo/dependencies.toml: each release of another Musher repository whose interfaces it vendors, or whose assets it fetches at test or build time, with the exact version it pins (EC-0032). Dependencies through a package or tool manager are read from that manager's manifest and are not listed. DEPS-02 checks a declaration against this schema.

dependencies.description: The vendored and fetched dependencies, at least one.

schema_version.description: Version of this file's shape. Always 1.

dependencies_schema.title: Dependencies declaration

body.description: Definition of the input types in the discussion form

labels.description: Labels that will automatically be added to discussions created with this template.

title.description: A default title that will be pre-populated in the discussion submission form.

allow_empty.description: An empty value is a deliberate, valid configuration. Requires default "" (ENVS-07).

capability.description: What the value reaches when it is not a Musher service: a runtime-capability token from the terminology, e.g. postgresql or object-storage (ENVS-18). It names what the code needs, never the resource that provides it. Never with target.

constraints.description: Range constraints the value must meet.

consumer.description: Which part of the product reads it. client means a browser bundle (ENVS-14).

consumers.description: The dev-environment stacks that read it.

default.description: The value the product uses when the variable is unset. It ships to production.

description.description: What the variable is for, in a sentence someone who has never seen it can act on: what breaks when the value is wrong, not what the name already says.

format.description: The shape of a string value. url marks an address the process connects to; an identifier shaped like a URL, such as an OIDC issuer or a JWT audience, leaves format unset and may use constraints.pattern (ENVS-12).

grammar_exempt.description: The naming grammar does not apply, because something outside the repository fixes the name. Requires grammar_exempt_reason (ENVS-07).

grammar_exempt_reason.description: Why the name is exempt from the grammar.

group.description: A heading the rendered environment file groups it under.

local_default.description: The value written into a developer's local environment file, correct only for a dev environment. A secret's may only be empty or address a loopback host (ENVS-06).

local_generate.description: Mint per-developer secret material into the local environment file instead of committing a value: hex:<bytes>, base64:<bytes> or base64url:<bytes>.

mirrored_in.description: Files, relative to the schema's directory, that repeat its local_default and must agree with it.

nested.description: Groups the binding into a nested settings model; its name then uses __ between group, sub-model and field (ENVS-13).

path.description: The secret-store path the value is read from, when not the schema's own infisical.path.

provider.description: The vendor whose API the code speaks for the capability, as a lower-case slug, e.g. stripe. Only with capability (ENVS-16).

python_field_name.description: The generated Python field name, when the lowercased variable name would collide with another attribute.

required.description: The product refuses to start without a value.

roles.description: The host roles whose rendered environment file carries it.

sensitivity.description: Who may see the value: public (anyone, including a browser), internal (the organization), confidential (people who operate the product), secret (a credential; only the process).

target.description: The other Musher service the value reaches, as <repository>#<interface>: the repository's name and the ID of the interface it serves, e.g. platform-api#public-http (ENVS-17). Never with capability.

type.description: The value's type. enum takes one of values; list is a comma-separated list, optionally of values.

values.description: The allowed values of an enum or list.

common_date.description: A calendar date in ISO 8601 form, YYYY-MM-DD.

coolifyEnv.description: The variables the deployment platform must hold before the process can reach its secret store.

generated.description: Code generated from the schema: pydantic for runtime python, ts for runtime sveltekit (ENVS-07).

framework.description: t3-core-client: inlined into the browser bundle at build time; t3-core-dynamic: read by the browser from the server at start, so one image serves every environment; t3-core-server: read on the server only.

output_path.description: Where the module is written, relative to the schema's directory.

infisical.description: Where the product's values are kept in Infisical, and how they reach the process.

delivery.description: container: the process fetches its values at start; coolify-env: the deploy copies them into the application's environment.

naming.description: The repository's own vocabulary for the naming grammar (ENVS-04, ENVS-09, ENVS-14).

client_prefixes.description: Prefixes that mark a variable a browser bundle reads. Defaults to VITE_ and PUBLIC_.

components.description: The component qualifiers a binding name may start with, without the trailing underscore, e.g. API, DATABASE, BRAVE_SEARCH. When declared, ENVS-04 asks every binding to start with one.

vendor_prefixes.description: Prefixes of vendor-owned names the grammar does not apply to, e.g. OTEL_ or AWS_.

prefix.description: An upper-case name prefix, ending in an underscore, e.g. VITE_.

reason.description: Why it is gone and what answers the question now. ENVS-05 prints it.

retired_on.description: The date the removal shipped, as a quoted YYYY-MM-DD.

apps.description: Every deployable that holds the value, this one included.

path.description: Where that deployable's copy is stored.

env_schema.description: An env.schema.yaml: the environment a product reads at runtime (<product>/env.schema.yaml), or the one its dev environment reads (.devcontainer/env.schema.yaml). EC-0020 describes every field; ENVS-03 checks a schema against this file, and ENVS-04 to ENVS-14 check what a JSON Schema cannot express. Draft-07 only: the checks validate with OPA, which ignores newer keywords.

bindings.description: Every variable the product reads, keyed by its name. ENVS-04 checks the names.

env_file.description: The file the process reads its environment from, when it reads one file rather than its inherited environment, e.g. .devcontainer/.env.

retired.description: Names the product deliberately stopped reading, with why; ENVS-05 refuses them again.

runtime.description: What reads the environment, as a lowercase token: python, sveltekit, node, go, rust, docker-compose. ENVS-07 ties the generated block to python and sveltekit.

service.description: The deployable the schema describes, e.g. platform-api; devcontainer for the dev environment's schema.

settings_file.description: Where a generated settings module is written, relative to the schema's directory; null when nothing is generated.

shared_with.description: Variables that hold the same value in several deployables; ENVS-07 and ENVS-08 check that every copy agrees.

vendor_passthrough.description: Variables a vendor library reads by its own name (OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT), passed through rather than declared as bindings; the naming grammar does not apply to them. A trailing * passes a whole prefix (INFISICAL_*).

common_repoPath.description: A path relative to a repository root, written with forward slashes and no leading slash or ./ prefix.

common_slug.description: A lower-case kebab-case identifier, e.g. github-actions.

audience.description: Who may build against it: internal or public, as in the identity declaration. IFACE-02 checks the token.

compatibility.description: What the producer promises about a change: an interface-compatibility token from the terminology, gated, versioned or lockstep. IFACE-02 checks the token.

definitions.description: The files that define it, relative to the repository root: a file, a directory ending in /, or a glob in which * stays within one path segment and ** crosses them, e.g. platform-api/contracts/events/*.schema.json.

delivered_by.description: The ID of the output in this declaration that delivers its definitions to consumers: a bundle, site or library (IFACE-06).

description.description: One line on what the interface is for and who builds against it.

docs.description: The document that says how to build against it, relative to the repository root, with an optional #anchor.

format.description: The format its definitions are written in: an interface-format token from the terminology, e.g. openapi, json-schema or protobuf. IFACE-02 checks the token.

generated.description: true when its definitions are generated from the product's code, so the contracts:generate task writes them and contracts:check proves they are current (IFACE-11).

id.description: The interface's name within this repository, unique, e.g. public-http. Other repositories address it as <repository>#<id>.

definition.description: Only in schema_version 1: a contract output's definition file. Declare an interface instead (EC-0030).

description.description: One line on what the output is for.

docs.description: The document that says how to consume it, relative to the repository root, with an optional #anchor, e.g. api/README.md#consuming.

format.description: Only in schema_version 1: a contract output's interface format. Declare an interface instead (EC-0030).

id.description: The output's name within this repository, unique, e.g. api-image.

kind.description: What kind of output it is: an output-kind token from the terminology, e.g. image, library, cli, bundle, site or vmimage. OUT-03 checks the token.

location.description: Where a consumer gets it: an image repository, a package name in its registry, or a release URL, e.g. ghcr.io/musher-dev/api.

publish_workflow.description: The filename of the workflow under .github/workflows that publishes it, e.g. publish-api.yml.

source.description: The file or directory it is built from, relative to the repository root, e.g. api/ or engineering-conventions/.

outputs_schema.description: A repository's .repo/outputs.toml: every output it publishes for other repositories or people to consume, where it is built from, which workflow publishes it, where consumers get it and where its consumption is documented; and, from schema_version 2, every interface its outputs deliver (EC-0030). OUT-02 checks a declaration against this schema.

interfaces.description: The interfaces this repository's outputs deliver: each surface another repository builds or runs against (EC-0030). Only in schema_version 2.

outputs.description: The outputs this repository publishes, at least one.

schema_version.description: Version of this file's shape. 2 adds [[interfaces]] and drops an output's format and definition; 1 is accepted until the contract kind's transition ends (decision 0022).

outputs_schema.title: Outputs declaration

common_repoPath.description: A path relative to a repository root, written with forward slashes and no leading slash or ./ prefix.

common_slug.description: A lower-case kebab-case identifier, e.g. github-actions.

release_record_schema.description: The release.json at the root of a bundle that delivers interfaces: which release it is, and each interface it delivers with the SHA-256 of each file (EC-0031). A consumer keeps it unchanged in its vendored copy (EC-0032), where DEPS-05 checks it against this schema.

commit.description: The full SHA of the commit the release was built from.

files.description: Each file of the interface, by its path from the bundle's root, with its SHA-256.

output.description: The id of the bundle output this record is the root of.

released_with.description: Other outputs cut by the same release, with the digest that identifies each, such as the image the interfaces describe.

repository.description: The producing repository's name on GitHub, without the organization.

schema_version.description: Version of this file's shape. Always 1.

tag.description: The release's tag, e.g. v0.36.1 or contracts/v0.36.1.

version.description: The release version, without a leading v.

release_record_schema.title: Release record

repository_schema.description: A repository's .repo/repository.toml: its name, the system it belongs to and the component it is within that system, its kind, the team that owns it, its lifecycle, its audience and its tier, and optionally its visibility. REPO-02 checks a declaration against this schema; REPO-03 checks the system, kind, lifecycle and audience against the registered values, and REPO-04 and REPO-07 to REPO-11 check the name. The optional layout table says where the product lives (EC-0018).

audience.description: Who the repository's outputs are for: internal or public. Not the same as its visibility on GitHub. REPO-03 checks the token.

component.description: What the repository holds within its system: the rest of its name, e.g. api.

kind.description: The repository's primary role, a registered kind, e.g. service. It selects the convention profile of the same name. REPO-03 checks the token.

layout.description: Where the repository keeps its product (EC-0018). REPO-14 asks for it; a repository without a product directory sets product to "".

product.description: The product directory: one path segment named after the repository, e.g. platform-api, or "" when the repository has no product directory.

root_exceptions.description: Root entries REPO-18 would report, each mapped to the reason it stays at the root, e.g. package.json = "Repository tooling only; the product has its own". REPO-19 checks each entry and reason.

lifecycle.description: Where the repository is in its life: experimental, production or deprecated. REPO-03 checks the token.

name.description: The repository's name on GitHub, without the organization: <system>-<component>, e.g. platform-api.

owner.description: The GitHub team that owns the repository, e.g. @musher-dev/platform. A team, never a person.

schema_version.description: Version of this file's shape. Always 1.

system.description: The registered system the repository belongs to, e.g. platform. REPO-03 checks the token.

tier.description: How much depends on the repository: 1 when its failure stops customers or the platform, 2 when it stops Musher's own work, 3 otherwise.

visibility.description: The repository's visibility on GitHub: public, private or internal. Optional. REL-18 asks a public repository, and one that does not declare it, to attest its release assets.

flag.description: A boolean. Claude Code also reads these words as one.

words.description: One string, separated by spaces or commas, or a list of strings.

skill_frontmatter_schema.description: The YAML frontmatter of a skill, .claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md (EC-0034). It accepts the fields of the Agent Skills specification and the fields Claude Code adds, and nothing else: anything of the repository's own, such as a version, goes under metadata. AGENT-10 checks a skill's frontmatter against this schema.

agent.description: The subagent a forked skill runs in. Claude Code.

allowed-tools.description: Tools the skill may use without asking. Agent Skills specification; Claude Code also accepts a list.

argument-hint.description: The arguments shown when the skill is invoked by name. Claude Code.

arguments.description: Named arguments, as a space-separated string or a list. Claude Code.

background.description: Whether a forked skill runs in the background. Claude Code.

compatibility.description: What the skill needs from its environment, at most 500 characters. Agent Skills specification.

context.description: fork: the skill runs in a subagent of its own. Claude Code.

description.description: What the skill does and when to use it, at most 1024 characters. An agent reads it to decide whether to load the skill. Agent Skills specification.

disable-model-invocation.description: true: only a person can invoke the skill, and no subagent can preload it (AGENT-14). Claude Code.

disallowed-tools.description: Tools the skill may not use. Claude Code.

effort.description: The effort level the skill runs at. Claude Code.

hooks.description: Hooks scoped to the skill. Claude Code.

license.description: The skill's license: a name or a bundled file. Agent Skills specification.

metadata.description: Anything else, as a map from string to string, such as a version. Agent Skills specification.

model.description: The model the skill runs with, or inherit. Claude Code.

name.description: The skill's name: lower-case letters, digits and single hyphens, at most 64 characters, equal to its directory's name (AGENT-11). Agent Skills specification.

paths.description: Globs naming the files the skill applies to, as a comma-separated string or a list. Claude Code.

shell.description: The shell the skill's commands run in. Claude Code.

user-invocable.description: false: the skill is hidden from the / menu. Claude Code.

when_to_use.description: More on when to invoke the skill, appended to the description. Claude Code.

skill_frontmatter_schema.title: Skill frontmatter

words.description: One comma-separated string, or a list of strings.

subagent_frontmatter_schema.description: The YAML frontmatter of a Claude Code subagent, a Markdown file under .claude/agents/ (EC-0034). It accepts the fields Claude Code reads and nothing else. AGENT-12 checks a subagent's frontmatter against this schema.

background.description: true: the subagent always runs in the background.

color.description: The subagent's colour in the task list and transcript.

description.description: When Claude should delegate to the subagent.

disallowedTools.description: Tools removed from the inherited or listed set.

effort.description: The effort level the subagent runs at.

experimental.description: Experimental settings, such as cacheTtl. Their names change between releases, so only the shape is checked.

initialPrompt.description: The first user turn when the subagent runs as the main session.

isolation.description: worktree: the subagent works in a temporary git worktree.

maxTurns.description: The most agentic turns before the subagent stops.

mcpServers.description: MCP servers, each a configured server's name or an inline definition.

memory.description: Where the subagent keeps persistent memory.

model.description: An alias, a full model ID, or inherit.

name.description: The subagent's identity. Claude Code skips a file whose name starts with a hyphen or holds a colon, which it reserves for plugins.

omitClaudeMd.description: true: the subagent starts without the CLAUDE.md files.

permissionMode.description: The permission mode the subagent runs in.

skills.description: Skills preloaded into the subagent's context, as a list or one comma-separated string, each the name of a skill in the repository (AGENT-13) that the model may invoke (AGENT-14).

tools.description: The tools the subagent may use, as a comma-separated string or a list. Omitted, it inherits every tool.

subagent_frontmatter_schema.title: Subagent frontmatter

banned_repository_tokens.common: Says who uses it, not what it holds; name what it holds.
banned_repository_tokens.legacy: Names a lifecycle, which changes while the name must not; drop the token and set lifecycle = "deprecated" in .repo/repository.toml.
banned_repository_tokens.misc: Says nothing about what it holds; name what it holds.
banned_repository_tokens.musher: The organization already says it; drop the token.
banned_repository_tokens.new: Names a lifecycle, which changes while the name must not; drop the token and set lifecycle = "experimental" in .repo/repository.toml.
banned_repository_tokens.old: Names a lifecycle, which changes while the name must not; drop the token and set lifecycle = "deprecated" in .repo/repository.toml.
banned_repository_tokens.repo: GitHub already says it is a repository; drop the token.
banned_repository_tokens.shared: Says who uses it, not what it holds; name what it holds.
banned_repository_tokens.util: Says nothing about what it holds; name what it holds.
banned_repository_tokens.utils: Says nothing about what it holds; name what it holds.
